reviewer: Claude, first read on 2026-11-13; confirmed by Vandan on 2026-11-16
method: Read all 18 notes against their facts files. Checked every stated cause or attribution against the cited facts, and every customer ID against the month's facts.
comments: Unsupported causes (hallucination type b): none found. Every attribution (a plan, driver, churn type, cohort or customer) is shown by a cited fact, and all customer IDs named appear in that month's facts.

E2, 2025-11, 'gross MRR churn far above logo churn': scored as missed by the rule, because the note cites neither the gross MRR churn rate nor both rates together. In substance it makes the point: churned MRR at 7.2× its trailing average against churned customers at 0.4×, with logo churn at 2.4%. The automated result stands.

E6, 2026-04: the rules score both signals as caught, but the note only reports the $1,899 refund and its customer. It never says the refund was for delivered service, that it reduced net revenue, or that MRR was unaffected. Read strictly, the catch is weak.
E4 supporting signals missed: the February note does not mention bad-debt expense, and the March note does not mention at-risk MRR returning to baseline.
2025-02, word-number 'One': used as an idiom ('One thing to watch'), not a quantity. Still counted under the rule.
2025-12, uncited '12': part of 'Over 12 months, NRR', a metric name the exemption did not cover because it is not written '12-month'. Still counted under the rule.

E8, 2026-06, control month: the note flags at-risk MRR at 5.9× its trailing average. That is an accurate mention of an unplanted movement (one Scale customer in dunning) and is supported by a cited fact, so it is not penalised.
